clue.text: Description of lob used for tennis

definitions.text: Description of lob used for tennis

parts.note: surface reading: someone is describing a lofted tennis shot
setter's reading: name the tennis event, played by pairs of a man and a woman, in which such shots are a staple

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a request for a shot description; really it wants the name of a tennis event. The wordplay is loose, so treat it as a whimsical cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixed doubles is the tennis event contested by teams each made up of one man and one woman.

clue.text: Daughter wears only nice pants, sitting on her arse

definitions.note: a phrase describing idleness, standing for the noun

indicators.note: whatever wears something has it around it, so one piece sits inside another
pants is British slang for rubbish, so these words are rendered worthless and remade

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A lazy daughter lounges about in her underwear all day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear being worn, but it is the anagram signal, and 'wears' puts D inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolency is laziness, the state of someone idly sitting around doing nothing.

clue.text: Supply Ecstasy and crack

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a crack is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Someone is dealing ecstasy and crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' suggests the drug alongside ecstasy, but here it means a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to provide or furnish someone with what they need.

clue.text: I might change answer — some solved it here recently

definitions.note: a description of the person, standing for the noun

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run lying across the words

parts.note: a run of letters straddling the four words

explanation.surface: A solver admits they may revise an answer they recently filled in.
explanation.definitionFit: A ditherer is an indecisive person who keeps changing their mind.

clue.text: Lack of cash concealed by trendy clothing

parts.note: something concealed by a cover is under it
in means fashionable
a vestment is a garment, especially a ceremonial robe

explanation.surface: Someone hides their poverty under fashionable clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Underinvestment is a failure to put enough money into something, a shortage of funding.

clue.text: The French aristocrat spared the guillotine, perhaps

parts.note: le is French for the
toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A French nobleman escapes execution during the Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To be let off is to be excused a punishment, as a condemned noble reprieved from execution.

clue.text: As you'll hear, teacher rewards hits for six

indicators.note: the listener is told to go by the sound of the words rather than their spelling

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
prizes are rewards

explanation.surface: A teacher gives prizes to pupils who hit sixes at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: To hit someone for six is a British cricket idiom for astonishing or overwhelming them; a six is a ball hit over the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: To surprise someone is to catch them unawares, which is what the cricketing idiom means.

clue.text: Lacking strength with low energy, revive

indicators.note: in a down entry, low means placed at the bottom, so this letter goes last

parts.note: weak means lacking strength; its E is moved
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A weak, tired person is told to perk up.
explanation.walkthrough: The E of WEAK drops down to the bottom of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To wake someone is to rouse them, bringing them back to an alert state.

clue.text: Bill and Ted entertain us on Japanese set

indicators.note: a host entertains guests by having them inside, so the outer pair holds the rest
in an across entry, one thing on another comes after it, so the first-named piece goes second

parts.note: an ad is a bill or poster
taken as written
J is the abbreviation for Japanese
taken as written, placed after the other piece

explanation.surface: The film duo Bill and Ted host a group on a Japanese film set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill and Ted' looks like the comedy film pair, but Bill is an advertisement here, and the two names together act as the host.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adjusted has been set, as a dial or clock is set to the right position.

clue.text: Sailor meets short goofy swinger

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the following word loses its final letter

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
zany means goofy; its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A sailor meets a small, silly person who is perhaps a party swinger.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarzan, the jungle hero, travels by swinging from vine to vine.

clue.text: Pass drinks, contents of beer bottle

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold something inside, so one piece encloses the other
the contents are what lies inside, so only the inner letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the inner letters of the word
laps means drinks, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to hand round drinks and the contents of a beer bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a noun after 'beer', but it is a verb: the beer's inner letters hold the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes by.

clue.text: Grass cut by schoolchildren unlikely to go back inside

indicators.note: a thing cut by another is split open with the second lodged in the gap

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a form is a school class, a group of pupils

explanation.surface: Grass is cut by schoolchildren unlikely to return indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' hints at an informer, matching the prison theme of the definition, but it is the plant. 'Inside' is slang for in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformed criminal has mended their ways and so is not expected to return to prison.

clue.text: Censor changed endings for The Omen as filmed

indicators.note: the word is altered into a different order of its letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: endings are final letters, so each word named gives only its last

parts.note: the final letters of each word

explanation.surface: A film censor alters the endings of the horror film The Omen.
explanation.definitionFit: On-screen describes what appears in a film or broadcast, as it was filmed.

clue.text: Revived bar opening in Cambridge, light blue

definitions.note: a ban brought back into force, i.e. a crackdown

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: the first letter
a lamp is a light
blue means sad or down

explanation.surface: A refurbished bar opens in Cambridge, decorated in the university's light blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Light blue is Cambridge University's colour, but here 'light' and 'blue' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A clampdown is a renewed crackdown, a ban strictly enforced once more.

clue.text: Payment to join navy's divers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: membership fees, short for subscriptions
second meaning: submarines, vessels of the fleet that dive

explanation.surface: A fee is charged to join the navy's diving team.
explanation.definitionFit: Subs is short for both subscriptions, the fees members pay, and submarines, the craft that dive underwater.

clue.text: Sedative lawyers munched on, back from rave

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers
bit on means chewed

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: Lawyers back from a rave chewed on sedatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbitone is a barbiturate drug formerly used as a sedative and sleeping pill.

clue.text: Lips are fixed around cold air hole

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, enclosing it
something fixed has been rigged or rearranged, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone's lips are set in place around a cold air vent.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiracle is a breathing opening, such as an insect's respiratory pore or a whale's blowhole.

clue.text: Bird that parrots accompany mainly keeps heading west

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means reading from right to left
the words keep the answer within them, holding it in their letters

parts.note: a run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A bird travels west with its parrot companions.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a starling famous for mimicking speech, just as parrots do.

clue.text: Fair guaranteed publicity

parts.note: an expo is an exhibition or trade fair
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A trade fair promises its exhibitors media coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is the state of being seen by the public, attention from the media.

clue.text: Porcelain in perfect condition available to order

parts.note: in mint condition means as new
on, as in on the menu, means available

explanation.surface: Fine china in pristine condition can be ordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Minton is a famous English make of fine china from Stoke-on-Trent.

clue.text: Nick's hours at work stretched by work left

indicators.note: something stretched is pulled apart to make room for extra material in its middle

parts.note: a shift is a period of working hours
op is short for opus, a work
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Nick's working day is lengthened by extra jobs he has been left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' reads as a man's name, but it is the verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, and shoplifting is stealing goods from a shop.

clue.text: First off the album!

parts.note: surface reading: the opening track of a record, announced with excitement
setter's reading: the Beatles record whose title track opens it and whose name ends in an exclamation mark

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark is part of the title: the Beatles' 1965 album's name carries one, and its title track is the first song.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles' album of that name opens with its own title song, so the first track shares the album's name.

clue.text: Cringe seeing nasty spill on playground

parts.note: rec is British short for recreation ground, a public playing field
an oil spill is a notorious kind of pollution

explanation.surface: Someone winces at a mess spilt on a playground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts the spill after the playground in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to flinch back in fear or disgust, as one does when cringing.

clue.text: Crumbs Joe gives dog

parts.note: both crumbs and cor are British exclamations of surprise
GI Joe is a nickname for an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone called Joe feeds biscuit crumbs to his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbs' reads as food scraps, but it is the mild British exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a small Welsh breed of dog, famously kept by the late Queen.

clue.text: Virtually nothing collected by charity that's closing

indicators.note: what is collected is gathered in and held inside the collector

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts to the poor
O looks like zero

indicators.note: the closing letter is the last one of the word

parts.note: the final letter, ignoring the apostrophe-s

explanation.surface: A closing charity has collected virtually nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and virtually both mean very nearly, but not quite.

clue.text: Key lingo for French food

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
argot is jargon or slang

explanation.surface: Someone needs the key words for ordering French food.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French term for snails, served as a delicacy in French cuisine.

clue.text: Score for nine is accepted by Countdown host: UNWITTING

parts.note: a nonet is a musical composition for nine players

indicators.note: something accepted is taken in, so the short word is placed inside the name

parts.note: Nick Hewer hosted Countdown, a British TV words-and-numbers quiz
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical piece for nine players is approved by a quiz host, who is clueless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests twenty or a game result, but here it is a piece of written music.
explanation.definitionFit: Being none the wiser means still not knowing or understanding something, i.e. unaware.
